note: queue_mail_language is a glue submodule of queue_mail with no config, no UI, no permissions. Its only effects are: (1) hook_queue_info_alter swaps the 'queue_mail' queue worker class to LanguageAwareSendMailQueueWorker (extends the parent SendMailQueueWorker); (2) it registers the service queue_mail.language_negotiator (QueueMailLanguageNegotiator extends core LanguageNegotiator) so queued mail is formatted in each mail's own langcode. It requires the language module and parent queue_mail. Because it has no config, medium/hard cases are grounded in the real live effects of the module being enabled: the queue_mail worker class and the negotiator service. Hard reset scripts uninstall the submodule (worker reverts to the parent class / service disappears) so verify FAILS on that state and PASSES only after the module is enabled. Cleanup leaves it enabled (its baseline for this suite).

evals.prompt: On a multilingual Drupal site using Queue Mail, queued emails are going out in the wrong language. Which submodule fixes this and what does it change?
evals.expected_output: Enable Queue Mail Language (queue_mail_language). It makes the queued send use each mail's own langcode instead of the cron/default language, by swapping the queue worker to a language-aware one. It requires the language module and queue_mail; there is nothing to configure.

evals.prompt: How does the queue_mail_language module change how the queue_mail queue is processed?
evals.expected_output: Its hook_queue_info_alter() sets the queue_mail queue's worker class to LanguageAwareSendMailQueueWorker (which extends the parent SendMailQueueWorker) and overrides setMailLanguage()/setActiveLanguage() to activate the mail's language during formatting.

evals.prompt: What does the queue_mail_language module require to work, and does it have any configuration of its own?
evals.expected_output: It requires the core language module and the parent queue_mail module. It has no configuration, no UI, and no permissions — enabling it is the whole setup.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the running site and state which PHP class processes the 'queue_mail' queue (the queue worker class handling queued emails).
evals.expected_output: The queue_mail queue worker class is Drupal\queue_mail_language\Plugin\QueueWorker\LanguageAwareSendMailQueueWorker (because queue_mail_language is enabled and its hook_queue_info_alter swapped it from the parent SendMailQueueWorker). Read via the queue worker plugin manager getDefinition('queue_mail').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the queue_mail_language module registers a service used to force the mail's language during queued sending. Inspect the running site's services and give the id of that language negotiator service.
evals.expected_output: The service id is queue_mail.language_negotiator (class QueueMailLanguageNegotiator, extends core LanguageNegotiator).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make sure queued emails are sent in each email's own language by enabling the appropriate Queue Mail submodule. After you are done, the queue_mail queue must be processed by the language-aware queue worker. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: queue_mail_language is enabled, so the queue_mail queue worker definition class is Drupal\queue_mail_language\Plugin\QueueWorker\LanguageAwareSendMailQueueWorker (e.g. `drush en queue_mail_language -y`).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, enable the Queue Mail Language module so that its language-negotiation service becomes available for formatting queued mail in the correct language. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: queue_mail_language is enabled, so the service queue_mail.language_negotiator is registered in the container (e.g. `drush en queue_mail_language -y`).
